text:
Anita (eng-infra): Heads-up — we're reworking node-pool strategy for GPU fleets. Main question: should we split pools by MIG vs time-sliced workloads, or try to serve both from a single mixed pool with labels? thinking about cluster-autoscaler behavior, binpacking, and cost visibility. any strong opinions? :thinking_face:
Sam (infra-sre): my 2c: split them. CA reacts to pod resource requests, but mixed pools make it hard to reason about fragmentation and spot pricing. Separate pools = easier autoscaler min/max for each workload class.
Jia (ml-infra): agree. ML teams have different p95 latency and preemption tolerance. MIG workloads (many small jobs) want high-density nodes with MIG profiles enabled. Time-slice/interactive jobs prefer full GPU or vGPU-style sharing — different device plugins and kubelet configs.
Dario (eng-runtime): +1. Also note that device plugins expose different resource names for MIG partitions, so scheduling logic is simpler when a nodepool is homogeneous. If you try to run MIG and non-MIG pods on same nodes you end up with complex admission logic and risk of unschedulable pods.
Anita (eng-infra): What about autoscaler settings? can we make CA respect GPU partitioning better, or do we just rely on labels/selectors?
Sam (infra-sre): CA doesn't understand MIG specifics beyond the resource names. Best practice: create nodegroups by GPU profile and label them e.g. `gpu.workload=ml-mig` and `gpu.workload=ml-full`. Then set CA min/max per nodegroup. Use `expander: least-waste` for packing small pods into MIG nodes.
Jia (ml-infra): example node labels we used: `gpu.type=nvidia-a100`, `gpu.profile=mig` and `gpu.workload=short-jobs`. Pod spec then uses `nodeSelector` + resource request like `requests: nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb: 1`. That avoids fractional GPU requests.
Dario (eng-runtime): sharing some snippets we use — nodepool config (kops/gke/eks style):

```yaml
nodeGroup: gpu-mig-a100
labels:
  gpu.type: nvidia-a100
  gpu.profile: mig
  gpu.workload: batch
autoscaling:
  minSize: 2
  maxSize: 20
  scaleDownDelay: 10m
taints:
  - key: dedicated-gpu
    value: "true"
    effect: NO_SCHEDULE
```

And a pod that targets MIG partitions:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: small-train
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu.profile: mig
  containers:
  - name: trainer
    image: redwood/ml-train:latest
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb: 1
```

Anita (eng-infra): nice. How do we handle cost visibility? Splitting pools increases granularity but also management overhead.
Sam (infra-sre): we tag nodepools with billing tags and surface per-pool token cost in the Console. For spot/spotlike instances, keep separate pools so we can have different fallback policies. Also set different rollout/eviction tolerances.
Jia (ml-infra): one more gotcha — MIG partitioning is tied to driver/firmware and requires nodes to be provisioned with the partitioning config at boot. If we spin up a node with wrong partitioning, it won’t be usable for the other pool without reprovisioning. That’s another reason to separate pools.
Dario (eng-runtime): about time-slicing (MPS/vGPU style): for T4s we sometimes run NVIDIA MPS and expose `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` but rely on in-container multiplexing. This works for low-intensity interactive workloads but you lose strong isolation and it's hard to autoscale for per-job granularity.
Anita (eng-infra): sounds like decision = create two node pools per SKU (mig vs full/share) with explicit labels + CA min/max. Anything else?
Sam (infra-sre): add a small "burst" pool with fast startup nodes for short jobs so the main MIG pool doesn't get overwhelmed by spikes. Set `maxSurge` on updates to avoid downtime.
Jia (ml-infra): we should add admission webhook that enforces `nodeSelector` for GPU pods so humans don't accidentally schedule incompatible pods. Simple deny + helpful message.
Dario (eng-runtime): agree. Also update our rollout docs with commands to reprovision nodes if partitioning changes.

Anita (eng-infra): perfect. i'll draft the PR: add new nodepool manifests, CA entries, and an admission check. will tag you all for review. :rocket:
